sodium.scope: Architecture and core rendering paths reviewed from exact source tag mc26.3-0.9.2, commit 03198cb36ab831c99694403d18e4cf4a1726df72. Reviewed worker executor, substantial render-section scheduling/cull lifecycle, meshing task, draw preparation/submission, and core occlusion traversal. GPU backends, all shader/math paths, every integration, and full equivalence remain pending.
mechanics: Treats terrain as persistent render sections with reusable geometry instead of rebuilding/drawing world blocks independently every frame. A section meshing task captures a pooled level slice, processes block/fluid models, collects block entities, and constructs visibility/translucency data.

Dedicated lower-priority mesh workers own reusable build contexts, avoiding a shared hot cache. The render thread can steal important jobs while waiting. Automatic worker count is capped and leaves CPU capacity for foreground work.

The section manager separates immediate, one-frame-deferred, and background work. It estimates CPU task cost and upload size/duration and budgets submissions against recent frame duration. Important nearby updates may block for timely presentation; deferred work is not simply discarded.

A separate cull worker computes local/regular/wide visibility trees during a controlled safe-read phase. Local results are rejected when the camera has changed since submission. The renderer picks the narrowest valid tree and falls back to a synchronous/out-of-graph traversal when no suitable result exists.

Occlusion traversal propagates reachable face-direction masks between adjacent sections using compact visibility data, perspective masks, outward-direction constraints, and cancellation checks. It maintains multiple conservativeness levels for camera-local versus wider reuse.

Region-level GPU geometry and cached multidraw batches combine section commands by terrain pass. Shared index buffers are reused where appropriate; translucent/indexed paths retain separate ordering needs.

Meshing can reuse unchanged translucent sorting/index data when allowed, with separate handling for forced sorting and removed geometry. Crashes are enriched with block, section, and captured-volume context.
Shutdown stops workers/culling, releases pending results and section/region/renderer resources. This lifetime management is part of the optimization's correctness, not optional cleanup.
risks: Geometry/batch caches must invalidate on section/model/resource changes. Stale async visibility can hide visible terrain unless validity tests and conservative fallbacks cover camera changes.
Snapshotting and per-worker caches require correct ownership; GPU submission/upload stays on the appropriate render path. Memory/upload pressure can dominate even if meshing is parallel.
Transparency order, dynamic sort triggers, custom models, OIT paths, resource reloads, and device/backends require separate detailed review.
The observed minimum upload budget constant is ten million nanoseconds while an adjacent comment says two milliseconds; research uses the literal value, not the inconsistent comment.
This is a substantial renderer replacement. A small cache or a collection of unrelated mods is not evidence of surpassing its performance.
validation: Compare terrain, fluids, lighting/AO, transparency, dynamic updates, outlines, and block entities across deterministic scenes. Stress camera turns, teleports, world/reload transitions, cancellation, and GPU memory pressure. Measure worker time, render-thread stalls, uploads, submissions, and frame intervals separately.
sodium.fit: Core high-value rendering architecture. Relevant lessons are persistent geometry, bounded scheduling, ownership, batching, and conservative visibility reuse; no Xe-Mod FPS gain is claimed.

async.scope: Focused upstream source review at bb4b149dd197b6583c81daaed752ae59aab21d41: ParallelProcessor, substantial ServerLevel hooks, server entry hook, task batching/ownership, and failure/shutdown paths. The many synchronization/entity compatibility mixins remain pending.
mechanics: Partitions eligible entities into synchronous and asynchronous sets using entity class/type rules, player/projectile/vehicle/portal exceptions, and opt-in compatibility annotations for nonvanilla entities.

Uses a measured smoothed per-item cost model to choose serial execution for small workloads and task sizes near a target batch duration for larger workloads. Groups entity work spatially by coarse chunk region before batching.

Runs worker batches with a countdown latch while the server thread ticks synchronous entities and helps drain pending work. While waiting for workers/locks, the server pumps chunk-source tasks to reduce deadlock risk from worker requests.

Adds foreground/background queues, a fixed worker pool, concurrent collections, queued block events, and optional asynchronous random-tick/spawn paths. Recorded tick timing is accumulated per entity type.

Individual entity/task exceptions are logged and execution continues; they are not transactionally rolled back. Shutdown signals synchronous handling, waits for workers, then clears queues/caches/statistics.
risks: Spatial grouping is not proof that entities/world mutations are independent. Shared blocks, inventories, RNG, events, and other mods need synchronization and ordering guarantees.
Replacing an ordered set of block events with a queue can change deduplication/order semantics. Thread-local RNG can change deterministic outcomes.
Logged-and-continued exceptions may leave partially mutated state. A discard-policy executor and shutdown races require liveness/coverage checks.
Class-keyed rule caches can be incorrect if one Java class represents multiple entity types with different configuration rules; cache keys must include every input.
validation: Compare complete world state, tick counts, event order, pickups, breeding, combat, RNG, inventories and chunk interactions with serial execution. Test exceptions, shutdown, rejected work, class/type rule changes, and deadlock/liveness under mod interactions.
async.fit: Server/integrated-server parallel simulation research; high compatibility/correctness complexity and no direct remote-client FPS guarantee.

vmp-fabric.scope: Focused source review from 26.3 branch commit 60888c93f4ccf593f1172b4ba71fa1a3b1cfa9ee: AreaMap, nearby entity tracking staging, entity-tracker position/listener hooks, and project architecture. Full network/chunk/playerwatching paths remain pending.
mechanics: Indexes player/entity tracking neighborhoods by chunk-coordinate keys, mapping each position to identity sets of relevant objects. Moving or changing a range adds/removes the difference between old/new square areas rather than testing every player/entity pair globally.
Pools identity sets, clears them on release, and optionally orders listener notifications by Chebyshev distance. Debug validation checks index membership invariants.

Nearby entity tracking keeps short-lived entities in a staging set before placing long-lived trackers into the more expensive area map. Position/listener hooks help avoid redundant checks and ensure first listeners receive tracking updates.
The wider project contains chunk sending, player watching, networking/event-loop and logging work; those paths are only inventoried here.
risks: Teleport, radius changes, removal, dimensions, and object identity must update every index exactly once. Exposing backing arrays requires stable iteration/ownership rules.
In the inspected tracker helper, getPreviousChunkPos packs prevX for both X and Z; callers need review and a differential test before labeling the practical impact.
Skipping normal tracked-status checks relies on callers establishing the equivalent range predicate. Staging migration and stop-tracking order require proof.
validation: Compare indexed candidate sets to brute-force range tests for random moves/radius changes, negative coordinates, teleports, removal, dimensions, and short-lived entities. Verify packet/listener transitions and pooled-set reuse.
vmp-fabric.fit: Server high-player-count candidate lookup/networking efficiency; useful indexing principles, not a general rendering replacement.

c2me-fabric.scope: Focused source review at c02dae000354e839956d1224ac830cb48c203d6d: module layout, prioritized/global executors, parallelism policy navigation, and asynchronous disk-read status. Worldgen, lighting, serialization, native/OpenCL modules and full dependency scheduler remain pending.
mechanics: Organizes chunk-processing work into separately controlled modules covering scheduling, chunk-system rewrites, serialization/I/O, lighting, worldgen threading fixes, and optional acceleration.

Uses a prioritized executor manager with configurable worker parallelism/priority and a separate single-thread scheduler. Dependencies and status transitions coordinate work rather than sending every world operation to an arbitrary thread pool.

The reviewed async disk-load status reads/converts chunk data, accumulates operations that must execute on the main thread, switches observation to that executor, and drains the deferred main-thread queue before finalizing.
Async-load failure retries with exponential backoff and then falls back to normal loading, also with bounded retries and diagnostic context.
risks: World generation often relies on shared caches/RNG or neighboring chunk state. Moving tasks requires complete dependency and ownership contracts.
Retry/fallback must not duplicate side effects from a partially completed load. Cancellation, unload and main-thread queue lifetime need inspection.
A source module existing does not mean the option is active or appropriate for client FPS; exact config and artifact build determine behavior.
validation: Compare generated/saved chunk contents across seeds and parallelism; test corrupted reads, retries, cancellations, unload races, queued side effects, worldgen extensions, and deterministic shutdown.
c2me-fabric.fit: Chunk generation/loading throughput and stutter research, mainly simulation/I/O; no blanket FPS claim.

iris.scope: Focused source review of 26.3 branch commit 671a5c87747d33983d7ed659461a64f46dfcb1f0: dimension pipeline manager, vanilla fallback, factory navigation, and renderer reload contract. Shader-pack parsing/compilation, all passes, shadows, uniform state, and compatibility remain pending.
mechanics: Creates/caches a world-rendering pipeline by dimension ID, resetting frame/time uniforms for new pipelines and rebuilding terrain when world rendering settings request it.
The pipeline factory selects a vanilla pipeline when no shader pack is active, and an Iris pipeline for an active pack with fallback on errors.

Destroying pipelines releases each dimension pipeline, clears the cache, nulls the active pipeline, and advances a renderer shader-reload generation counter. Resets bound texture state to avoid references to destroyed targets.
The vanilla pipeline restores ordinary world-render settings and supplies no custom shadow pass; shader loading is distinct from terrain CPU optimization.
risks: GPU state/texture/framebuffer lifetimes and immediate re-preparation after destruction must stay consistent. Multiple dimensions can share underlying pipeline data and renderer override generations.
Shader packs add GPU/CPU work and change visuals. Having a shader loader installed does not establish an FPS improvement with shaders disabled.
validation: Check shader-disabled/failed-load fallback, dimension switches, reloads, shared pipeline lifetimes, texture bindings, renderer shader generations, and every active pass.
iris.fit: Shader integration/lifecycle research; current Xe-Mod requirement excludes external shaders.

lcull.scope: All five reconstructed source files reviewed, including the nested Fabric initializer.
mechanics: Caches six normalized frustum planes and precomputes bias values for eight cube half-extent buckets. Entity rendering uses center/half-extent tests through a frustum duck interface, plus margins and leash-holder bounds.
Players and selected exempt/nearby display cases retain normal handling. Ordinary Frustum.isVisible directly calls the existing intersection AABB test.
Replaces camera-cube offsetting with a bounded, growing-step loop capped by iteration count and total offset. Also suppresses specific out-of-view-range log messages.
risks: The largest extent bucket has half-size eight regardless of larger input bounds. For inputs larger than that, it can under-enclose geometry and falsely reject a visible object.

The bounded camera-offset loop can stop before the required cube containment condition holds. Float normalization, degenerate planes, reload/set, custom render bounds and leashes require differential checks.
Using an enclosing cube for smaller boxes can add false positives; that preserves visibility but reduces rejection efficiency.
validation: Compare all visibility decisions to the original across large displays/entities, exact frustum boundaries, non-finite bounds, camera cubes, matrix changes, leashes, and randomized AABBs.
lcull.fit: Interesting plane precomputation, but observed approximate/capped behavior cannot be assumed visually exact.

vo-camera-culling.scope: All five reconstructed Java classes reviewed.
mechanics: After vanilla entity eligibility succeeds, raycasts from the camera to center/head/feet and, for wider entities, four middle-height corners. If all tested points are blocked, rejects rendering.

Exempts the local player, vehicles/passengers, glowing entities, near objects, and invalid bounds. Block entities are rejected when all six neighboring blocks are solid-rendering or the center ray is blocked.
Uses visual block clipping with fluids ignored and tracks rendered/culled counters. A class-existence guard catches only a basic API mismatch.
risks: Blocked sample points do not prove that every part of an entity/rendered model is hidden. Transparent visual shapes, extended block-entity effects, and beams can still be visible.
The source constructs ray vectors/clip contexts and performs several raycasts per query; a zero-allocation/performance claim requires actual profiling and JIT analysis.
A generic class-existence guard does not establish method signatures or semantic compatibility.
validation: Test partial visibility through gaps/glass, large/custom geometry, beams/signs/chests, glowing outlines, camera turns, raycast workload, and allocation profiles.
vo-camera-culling.fit: Occlusion by sparse sampling can improve some scenes but is not a proof of unchanged visuals.

rabbit-pathfinding-fix.scope: All eight reconstructed Java classes reviewed; mixin superclass helpers only expose inherited state.
mechanics: Changes path stuck-timeout accounting to game ticks with bounded/default node timeouts. The hook targets general PathNavigation, not only rabbit navigation.
Adjusts rabbit jump power based on collisions/target height/speed, avoids redundant speed-modifier writes, and adds a look-around goal.
Garden-raiding goal changes reach/path recalculation and waits for a jump to finish before continuing crop interaction. Client model setup applies explicit head/hop/idle animation state.
risks: Changes navigation, movement, goals and animation behavior. General navigation timeout interception can affect mobs beyond rabbits.
validation: Check blocked/zero-speed paths, carrot raids, jump timing/heights, other mob navigation, and client animation equivalence to intended fixes.
rabbit-pathfinding-fix.fit: AI/animation bug fixes with behavior changes, not a generic performance algorithm.

skeleton-ai-fix.scope: All seven reconstructed Java classes reviewed; tag resource/library behavior is externally supplied.
mechanics: For tagged skeletons at entity-tick end, forces bow-goal strafing time to Integer.MIN_VALUE to suppress the usual strafing behavior.
Recalculates attack interval from difficulty, a configured multiplier, and an eased fraction of squared distance relative to attack radius. Closer targets can produce faster attacks.
An entity-type tag controls participation; loader callbacks/configuration register the event path.
risks: Changes combat/movement behavior and checks each eligible entity every tick. Zero radius or extreme config values need handling.
validation: Test skeleton variants/tag membership, difficulty, attack interval boundaries, no/near/far targets, and actual movement/attack outcomes.
skeleton-ai-fix.fit: Combat AI behavior fix, not unchanged-behavior optimization.

serveraddressspacefix.scope: All nine reconstructed Java classes reviewed.
mechanics: Removes literal ASCII space characters from server addresses in direct-join screen initialization/selection/removal, server-add input, and ServerData construction when enabled.

Loads optional config-library settings on client startup, watches the config directory from a virtual thread, and swaps a volatile settings instance on relevant changes. Saves on shutdown and migrates an old config path.
risks: Removes interior spaces as well as trailing whitespace, and does not normalize other whitespace. A hook executing before settings initialization can see a null settings instance.
Migration deletes the old file before writing the new one. Watcher/library thread safety and shutdown lifetime need checks.
validation: Test leading/interior/trailing spaces and other whitespace, early ServerData construction, absent config library, file migration failures, and live reload/shutdown.
serveraddressspacefix.fit: Connection input cleanup; no rendering performance benefit.

mechanics: After the multiplayer screen refresh creates/shows the new screen, obtains its server list through an accessor and copies the old list's scroll amount.
risks: Assumes the current screen is the expected mixin target and refresh is immediate. List lengths can differ after refresh, requiring scroll clamping.
validation: Check long/short lists, refresh while screens change, added/removed servers, and accessor/hook signature compatibility.
idontwannascrollagain.fit: UI state preservation; not an FPS optimization.

serverlens.scope: All four reconstructed source files reviewed, including the nested ping callback; renderer body and core ping lifecycle inspected separately.
mechanics: Debounces address-bar changes for 500 milliseconds on a single daemon scheduler and assigns request IDs so stale ping results can be rejected.
Runs the normal status pinger until completion, polling its tick every 50 milliseconds and cleaning connections in finally. Returns status/MOTD/player count/ping and favicon to the client thread.

The direct-connect screen draws the preview, maps ping to bar icons, validates/caches favicon bytes, and replaces/closes uploaded favicon textures when data changes. Scheduler shuts down on client stop.
risks: The shown polling loop has no own deadline; it depends on the underlying pinger to finish or interruption. The request-ID check occurs before queuing a client callback, so another address edit before callback execution needs a second stale-result check.
Screen-close texture cleanup and cancellation races require verification; frame-by-frame address polling adds UI work.
validation: Test rapid edits, stalled/unknown servers, cancellation, stale responses arriving during client-thread delay, screen close/reopen, invalid icons, and texture/thread cleanup.
serverlens.fit: Direct-connect UI feature with useful debounce/lifecycle patterns; not gameplay FPS optimization.
